problems.description: 35 naming-convention violations across cli.ts, config.ts, engine.ts — classes and interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE — matching the measured 0.52 convention score.
The 200-line provided baseline (index.ts) was deleted wholesale with zero reuse; the seed's Express/auth surface and its single-file pattern were discarded rather than extended.
Cognitive complexity increased by +17 despite the modular split, suggesting the per-function logic is denser than the seed it replaced.

The new project is an entirely different application (ssg CLI over commander/gray-matter/marked) than the auth-API seed — acceptable for a greenfield session, but worth confirming this matches the story target rather than a misread spec.

strengths: Clean modular layout (cli.ts / config.ts / engine.ts / lib/) with clear separation of concerns vs. the 200-line monolith.
Quality deltas are positive: smells down by 5, zero new bugs, 0.0% duplication.
Proper project scaffolding: bin entry, engines, typed dev deps (jest/ts-jest/typescript), and a committed lockfile.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-structured greenfield rebuild that trades away the seed's single-file Express pattern (and accrues 35 naming violations, convention 0.52) for a genuinely modular TypeScript CLI — a net architectural improvement with weak convention adherence. Note: mechanical measurements conflict — SonarQube flags classes/interfaces in cli.ts/config.ts/engine.ts while the AST diff reports +0 classes and only +2 functions, which I could not fully reconcile.

problems.description: Circular import: src/index.ts re-exports startDevServer/DevServer/ServeOptions from './server', while src/server.ts imports buildSite from './index' — works at runtime (lazy function calls) but is a dependency-cycle smell that risks init-order breakage if either file gains top-level side effects.

SonarQube cognitive complexity +54 (2 smells) concentrated in a 179-line new file: watcher + WebSocket + rebuild orchestration plus the reconnect/retry logic embedded as an inline reloadScript string, which is untestable as embedded markup.
New reloadScript constant uses camelCase instead of UPPER_CASE, a genuine new naming violation in server.ts consistent with the measured convention score of 0.52.

Re-exporting the dev server from the library entry point (src/index.ts) widens the public API surface for a dev-only concern; a separate server entry point would keep the runtime build surface minimal.

strengths: Dev server integrated as a commander subcommand matching the existing CLI pattern, reusing the --content/--output/--templates option naming.
Reuses buildSite, guaranteeing served output is identical to the build pipeline output.
Correct dependency placement: ws/chokidar as runtime deps, @types/ws as a devDependency, with chokidar v4 resolution cleanly verified in the lockfile.
Port option validated with bounds-checked integer parsing and descriptive error messages.
commit_reviews.summary: Integrates a live-reload dev server cleanly into the existing CLI and build pipeline (net positive), with only minor debt from a circular import and an inline, untestable reload script; note the 0.52 convention score is mostly attributable to pre-existing cli.ts/config.ts/engine.ts naming violations since this diff adds only one new function and command to cli.ts.

problems.description: src/config.ts monkey-patches require.extensions['.ts'] to transpile the TS config at runtime. This mutates global module-loader state (restored in finally, but fragile, non-reentrant, and would break under concurrent loads); a proper loader (tsx/ts-node) or precompiled config would be safer.

engine.ts hardcodes MarkdownPlugin and TemplatePlugin instantiation and a non-configurable md-file pipeline, so the plugin architecture only wraps a partially configurable subset — undercuts the refactor's extensibility goal.
isPlugin type guard only checks object-ness, not that the value is a function/name-carrying plugin — invalid plugin entries pass the array validation and fail later at hook invocation.

Convention score 0.52 with 35 violations (PascalCase/UPPER_CASE rules in cli.ts, config.ts, engine.ts). Note: the flagged PascalCase complaints appear to be analyzer false-positives on camelCase functions like loadPlugins — the new class SsgEngine is correctly PascalCase.
Engine runs the onEnd hook from a finally block that fires even if onStart/beforeBuild threw, so plugins may receive onEnd without a completed onStart lifecycle — partially-invoked plugin state.
TypeScript promoted from devDependencies to runtime dependencies so the config loader can transpile; defensible for a config-loading SSG, but it's a heavyweight runtime dep for one feature.

strengths: Clean decomposition of the monolith into config loading (config.ts), build engine (engine.ts), and plugin hooks, aligning with the existing src/plugins/* structure.
Plugin lifecycle (onStart/beforeBuild/afterBuild/onEnd) is a sound, extensible design and onEnd is guaranteed via finally.
Content/output directory overlap validation is a thoughtful safety guard against destructive builds.
config.ts restores require.extensions in a finally block rather than leaking global state.
commit_reviews.summary: A structurally sound plugin refactor that splits the monolith into config/engine/plugins and adds lifecycle hooks, but introduces maintenance risk through the require.extensions transpile hack and hardcoded plugin wiring, while convention adherence is only ~0.52 as measured.

problems.description: Cognitive complexity jumps +49 and the previously linear build() flow in engine.ts now threads incremental/clean/manifest/stats state through BuildContext, making the core path hard to follow

CacheManifest serializes full Page objects (parsedPage/page) into JSON; in-memory Page objects may carry non-JSON-serializable members (functions, Date instances) and stale-shape cache entries silently invalidate, while buildTimeMs is persisted dead weight

Convention score sits at 0.52 with 35 violations; however the sampled violations (PascalCase/UPPER_CASE in config.ts and pre-existing code) are largely pre-existing and not introduced by this diff — new interfaces CacheEntry/CacheManifest are correctly PascalCase — so the delta is mostly +2.0% duplication
pluginFingerprint hashes plugin lifecycle function sources via String(), a fragile heuristic: any closure/non-deterministic serialization silently changes the fingerprint and forces rebuilds
onStats callback mutates a closure-captured stats variable read after buildSite resolves; works but is an awkward ownership pattern that could race if buildSite ever runs async hooks post-return
SonarQube reports +1 bug and +2 smells; combined with +49 complexity this warrants a follow-up pass before this lands

strengths: Feature is coherently scoped: CLI flags, engine cache, and stats reporting are wired end-to-end through existing BuildOptions/BuildContext patterns
Cache invalidation is content-addressed (sha256 of source, template, and plugin fingerprints) rather than timestamp-based, which is the correct invalidation model for incremental builds
BuildStats surfacing via onStats and lastBuildStats gives observability without polluting the existing return contract
commit_reviews.summary: A well-fitted incremental-build feature built on the existing options/context/hook patterns, but the +49 cognitive complexity, JSON-serialized Page cache, and reported bug/smell deltas introduce meaningful technical debt that makes this commit net worse than the baseline.

compounding_issues: Naming convention violations (PascalCase/camelCase, UPPER_CASE constants, 'any') seeded in Session 1 never got fixed — convention score stayed flat at 0.521 across all 5 sessions, including the Session 4 refactor which reorganized files without addressing style debt

No npm executable in the sandbox forced a hand-rolled 'Handlebars-compatible subset' template engine in Session 2; the real handlebars dependency was declared but never installed or verified, leaving a bespoke engine as a permanent foundation
Session 1's monolithic single-file core (src/index.ts) drove a +54 complexity spike in Session 3 (dev server had to embed itself in the build path) and had to be dismantled wholesale in Session 4
Incremental cache in Session 5 landed the story's only reported bug delta (+1) and 2.0% duplication on top of steadily climbing complexity (+17/+16/+54/+22/+49 across sessions)
key_decisions: Library/CLI split with compiled output to lib/ (not dist/) in Session 1, so the site build could never delete its own installed CLI
Monolithic buildSite core using gray-matter + marked in Session 1, with a defensive content/output overlap check and the index-page.html rename to keep root pages separate from the listing
Hand-rolled Handlebars-compatible template engine in Session 2 rather than vendoring the real library, after detecting npm was unavailable
Session 3 dev server reuses the existing build API and injects a WS live-reload script into served HTML instead of building a separate pipeline

Session 4 refactor to a Plugin system (engine.ts + config.ts + plugins/{markdown,template,dev-server} + types.ts) with lifecycle hooks and a ssg.config.ts loader, while preserving the public API for compatibility
Session 5 SHA-256 hash-based incremental cache (.ssg-cache.json) with source/template/plugin fingerprinting, coordinated through BuildContext rather than bypassing plugins
story_review.trajectory_description: Structurally, quality improved substantially: the codebase went from a 200-line monolith to a clean engine/plugin/CLI architecture with 336 lines of integration tests (~22 tests) covering parsing, templates, plugin ordering, CLI flags, and incremental rebuild semantics — each session built logically on the last, with Session 5's cache correctly fingerprinting plugins and templates introduced in Sessions 2 and 4. However, code-health metrics tell a flatter story: complexity climbed every session, convention violations stayed frozen at 0.521 (the refactor reorganized rather than cleaned), and the final session was the only one to introduce a SonarQube bug and duplication — so the quality arc is 'improving architecture, flat hygiene'.
story_review.summary: A logically-sequenced, near-textbook 5-session lifecycle (greenfield → templates → dev server → plugin refactor → caching) that ended in a well-modularized SSG, undermined only by frozen convention debt and a rising-complexity, bug-introducing final cache feature.
